title: Implement Eclipse Jetty core HTTP handler adapter

timeline.body:
This provides an implementation of a HTTP Handler Adaptor that is coded directly to the Eclipse Jetty core API, bypassing any servlet implementation.

Fixes #32035

timeline.body: @lachlan-roberts @sbordet Any ideas on how to make this release a bit less ugly?  I want to release after onNext returns, but the only hooks I have is the next call to onNext or the final call to onComplete

reply.body: @lachlan-roberts I think you are correct.  It is the implementation of `onNext(Databuffer db)` that is responsible to do the release.   I bit of a strange contract, but I can see that is how they are doing it elsewhere in the code.   Good one! Thanks!

timeline.body: @lachlan-roberts @sbordet  previous comment still applies to this version.  This is a little better, but holds onto a databuffer until the next one arrives, which by definition prevents the previous buffer being reused.  We really want to release after onNext has been called.

This `Lock` got my attention because pessimistic locking is usually not the first go-to method in Reactive Streams. Instead it's usually some sort of optimistic locking with a CAS loop.

That said, the lock protects 2 critical sections that represent quick state checks and updates. There is precedent for that sort of things, e.g. in `Reactor`, so in that case I think it is fine (although care will need to be exercised if the code is modified or new usage of the lock is introduced).
this is more problematic, as `n` can be an "unbounded request" (`Integer.MAX_VALUE`) and `this.requested` can overflow to negative.

reply.body: I updated with the change suggested by @simonbasle not the `Math.addExact`. So once it reaches `Long.MAX_VALUE` it is considered an "unbounded request" and no longer decrements `this.requested` when demanding.

timeline.body:
I'm not entirely sure how it translates in terms of `getDelegate().demand()` calls, but if the requested amount is unbounded, this decrement shouldn't happen.

with the above suggested change, unbounded request amount (`n == Integer.MAXVALUE` at any point) leads to `this.requested == Long.MAX_VALUE` so if that's the case the `this.requested--` decrement should be skipped.
same as above, this should take the "unbounded request" scenario (in the Reactive Streams sense) into consideration
I'm not sure why `doCommit` is called here. Typically it's called once for a response, and it's already done in the base class before the call to `writeInternal`.
This is supposed to flush after each nested `Publisher`, e.g. to ensure events in SSE stream are sent at the right time. Is there anything to ensure that? Nothing obvious that I see.

reply.body:
Jetty writes at this level are non-buffering.  Any aggregation that might require flushing is done at a higher level.     Now, we might actually buffer (e.g. if sitting in a flow control congested HTTP/2 stream), but if so, then flushing is not going to help.

The only time we really need a flush semantic is if there is no content at all, then we will write an empty buffer, so that at least the HTTP response headers are generated etc. So perhaps this method needs to detect if the body was actually empty, in which case an empty buffer should be written
